reference.text: By this, he seemed to mean, not only that the most reliable and useful courage was that which arises from the fair estimation of the encountered peril, but that an utterly fearless man is a far more dangerous comrade than a coward.

underlines.text: was not a sentiment; but a thing simply useful to him, and always at hand upon all mortally practical occasions

reference.text: Yet, for all his hardy sobriety and fortitude, there were certain qualities in him which at times affected, and in some cases seemed well nigh to overbalance all the rest.

underlines.text: shall hereafter ascribe high qualities, though dark
